subject: Request: trial & sandbox extension — API shim blocking demo
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orbitric.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Integration blocker — need a short extension + sandbox credits

Hey Marcus,

Quick one — our backend team hit a blocker with the API shim during the connector work (see Jira ORB-5678). The error is causing the message schema negotiation to fail intermittently; engineers are stalled and we can't get the end-to-end demo into a stable state.

We have the stakeholder demo tentatively on Sep 10 but at this rate it will be noisy. Would Redwood be able to extend our trial window by ~30 days and top up the sandbox with ~$2k of credits so our engineers can run longer QA cycles?

I attached a short clipped log (error_log_snip.txt) and a 90s screen capture (demo_recording_trim.mp4) showing the failure. If you need more detail I can loop in Anya (CTO) and our lead eng.

Appreciate any help — this deal is important for us to prove the flow.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Product Manager, Orbitric
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orbitric.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration blocker — need a short extension + sandbox credits

Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts.

Sorry to hear you hit that. Can you confirm whether the failures are reproducible in your environment with a fixed seed (we ask to rule out client-side variability)? Also: which model variant and sequence lengths are you testing on? That helps Kimberly estimate cost for the sandbox bump.

I'm looping in Marissa (CS) and Kimberly (SE) to get operational and credits guidance. We typically approve extensions for integration blockers; want to make sure we align on the amount and timeline.

Short-term: we can provision a temporary sandbox credit pool while we triage. I'll get back with a concrete offer by EOD tomorrow after we review your logs.

Best,
Marcus
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orbitric.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration blocker — need a short extension + sandbox credits

Thanks Marcus — reproduces consistently on our staging cluster when we hit payloads with nested metadata (longer sequence lengths ~2.5k tokens). We're testing against gpt-like-open-7b variant in your catalog.

Error snippet included in error_log_snip.txt; in short, the shim drops a portion of the KV during retry, causing a mismatch on subsequent calls. Our eng lead notes it looks like a tokenization boundary issue when the prefix cache is used.

Attached a 90s clip of the demo failure. If you can provision a short runway extension and a $2k sandbox credit, we can get back to a clean demo in ~2 weeks.

Samir
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Integration blocker — need a short extension + sandbox credits

Marissa / Kimberly — forwarding Orbitric's ask (see attached logs). Deal: ORB-3245 (HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ORB-3245).

Request: 30-day trial extension + $2k sandbox credits while their engineers resolve the shim drop; region: US; model: open-7b variant; token profile: spikes to ~2.5k.

Questions for approvals:
- Marissa: OK to authorize the extension + credit as a one-time make-good for an integration blocker?
- Kimberly: Can we confirm $2k is sufficient for their typical test volume with the stated model? If not, what would be a safe amount?

If both green, I'll reply to Samir with the formal extension and attach SOC2 snapshot they asked for.

Thanks — Marcus
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Integration blocker — need a short extension + sandbox credits

Marcus — approved.

Approve 30-day trial extension and a $2,000 sandbox credit as a one-time runway assist for ORB-3245. Please log the credit against the deal in HubSpot and set the credit expiry to 30 days from when it's applied.

Kimberly — if you think $2k won't cover their QA runs for 2 weeks given the open-7b workload at 2.5k tokens, propose the amount now; otherwise we'll stick to $2k. Also offer a 60-min troubleshooting session with SE to accelerate the unblock — that usually helps.

I'll attach SOC2_snapshot.pdf for their compliance review.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orbitric.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-06T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration blocker — need a short extension + sandbox credits

Samir — good news. We reviewed your logs and approved the request.

What we can do:
- 30-day trial extension, moving your expiry to 2027-10-07
- $2,000 sandbox credit applied to ORB-3245 (expires 30 days after issuance)
- SOC2 snapshot attached for your compliance team (SOC2_snapshot.pdf)
- Kimberly will schedule a 60-minute troubleshooting session with your engineering lead — Kimberly, can you propose 2 slots next week?

I'll record the credit in HubSpot here: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ORB-3245 and will mark this as a one-time make-good tied to the integration blocker (ticket ORB-5678).

Let me know if you'd like us to extend the sandbox window further depending on the remediation progress.

Best,
Marcus
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
